Lengiz “Books” poster

Alexander Rodchenko’s advertisement for the Leningrad State Publishing House, with Lilya Brik calling out the slogan, is the most copied image of Soviet constructivism.

Source
Wikipedia: Alexander Rodchenko
Creator
Alexander Rodchenko
Made
1924 (Wikipedia); 1925 in some dealer and reproduction listings
Style
Constructivism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Agitational, declarative, photographic
Evidence
Based on text sources only. No museum record with an image of a printed copy was found: MoMA refuses automated access, and the Art Institute of Chicago and the V&A do not list the poster. Search results describe a photomontage and gouache design in a private collection, which may differ from any printed version.
Reviewed

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

No image of an identified copy was inspected. Treat the visual description as unverified until a museum record is checked.

Context

Wikipedia calls it “likely his most famous poster, an advertisement for the Lengiz Publishing House sometimes titled ‘Books’”, made in 1924, with the slogan “книги по всем отраслям знания” (books in all branches of knowledge). Wikipedia.

The woman in the photograph is Lilya Brik. Franz Ferdinand based the cover of their 2005 album You Could Have It So Much Better on the poster. Wikipedia.

Why it belongs

The poster’s long afterlife in album covers and advertising shows that its combination of a cut-out photograph and constructivist type is how many people recognize the style today.

What to review next
